text: {"domains":{"block_M":[64,128,256],"block_N":[64,128,256],"block_K":[32,64,128],"num_stages":[1,2,3,4],"threads":[128,256],"swizzle":[0,8,16,32,64]},"shared_memory_limit":32768,"weights":{"traffic":1.2,"launches":0.6,"pipeline":1,"footprint":1.2},"rationale":"Baseline attempt-00 chose 128x64x64, stage 1, 256 threads, swizzle 0, and passed SMT/numerical/compile with smem exactly at the 32768 hard cap (98 regs, 2 blocks/SM) at 3560.55 us simulated. With M=N=K=4096, all tiles divide. Changes: (1) Add swizzle 8-64 (drop 4, since with 32-64 block_M tile rows and large N there are many tile columns, so panel locality should vary meaningfully) to test the serpentine reuse hypothesis; baseline was row-major per instructions. (2) Add block_M=256 and block_N=256 to probe larger tiles, while block_K=128 allows the 32768 cap to be satisfied only via small complementary tiles (estimate 2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages must stay <=32768), so HiGHS can pick large-tile/small-K or small-tile/large-K trade combinations. (3) Threads narrowed to 128/256 since 64 competes poorly with 256 threads for a 4096^3 GEMM and identical tile/stage/swizzle ties were observed for 128/256. (4) Weights: raise footprint to 1.2 because baseline sat exactly at cap with 2 blocks/SM and stage 1; raising traffic to 1.2 to stress locality as swizzle varies, while lowering launches to 0.6 because block counts (4096/tile)^2 already amortize well and we want the objective to differentiate traffic/locality against footprint. Stage 4 retained for consideration within the cap. Next hypothesis: swizzled panels with matched 128/256 tile pairs and moderate stages reduce simulated DRAM traffic vs row-major; if simulator traffic does not drop with swizzle, revert swizzle to [0] and instead push block_N or block_K upward. Metal validation covers exact source/config/TIR only, not the CUDA binary; GB10 timings are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements, and no global optimality is claimed."}
